apps.description:
Bling is a chat app that connects directly to the other people you are
talking to. There is no account, no sign-up and no relay server: messages
travel over a libp2p swarm between the devices themselves.

How it works:

* Your identity is a key pair generated on the device and stored locally.
* Peers find each other on the local network, or you paste an invite address
  to connect across networks.
* Each room is a gossipsub topic, so everyone in the room sees the same
  messages.

Things worth knowing:

* Rooms are open to anyone who knows the room name.
* History is kept on the device only, and the last 300 messages per room are
  kept.
* On Android 17 and later, the app asks for local network access so it can
  reach peers on your Wi-Fi.
* Notifications only appear when the app is in the background.
* Nothing is stored on a server, because there is no server.

Bling is free software under the MIT license.
